recognize_zh: 血液抹片右側可見一顆接近紅血球大小、含紫紅色顆粒的巨大血小板，與畫面中央正常大小的小血小板形成對比；但本圖只見一顆巨血小板且解析度低，無法看出「大量」巨血小板。
features: One giant platelet at right, approaching the diameter of an adjacent red cell, with a central purple granulomere and pale peripheral hyalomere
A normal-sized small platelet in the center for comparison
Two neutrophils (one band-like, one segmented) with normal granulation and no visible Döhle-like inclusions
Normocytic red cells with central pallor
Low image resolution limits assessment of platelet number and granule detail
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a giant platelet approaching red cell size with preserved purple granulation, contrasting with a normal-sized platelet nearby. Two neutrophils show normal granulation without obvious Döhle-like cytoplasmic inclusions, and red cells are unremarkable. Only a single giant platelet is present in this low-resolution field, so the degree of macrothrombocytopenia cannot be assessed. The finding is compatible with an inherited macrothrombocytopenia such as Bernard-Soulier syndrome, which requires absent ristocetin-induced agglutination and reduced GPIb-IX-V expression by flow cytometry for confirmation.

ddx.vs: Giant platelets are accompanied by Döhle-like basophilic inclusions in neutrophils, and ristocetin agglutination is normal.
Large platelets are pale gray and agranular rather than normally granulated.
Young large platelets are present but not consistently red-cell sized, platelet function testing is normal, and there is no lifelong family history.
